floor-repair/longboat-key.title: Floor Repair Longboat Key FL | Condo Leaks & Cracked Tile
floor-repair/longboat-key.description: Floor repair on Longboat Key, mostly condo water damage and cracked tile in guest-facing units in Bay Isles and Country Club Shores, 2026 pricing.
floor-repair/longboat-key.h1: Floor Repair for Longboat Key Condos and Villas
floor-repair/longboat-key.lede: Longboat Key repair calls tend to be higher stakes than a typical mainland fix, since most of what we're patching sits in a rental-ready or guest-facing condo rather than an everyday family room.
floor-repair/longboat-key.capsule: Floor repair on Longboat Key concentrates in two patterns: water damage from a neighboring unit in a condo tower and cracked or hollow-sounding tile in a guest-facing rental or second home. A typical cracked-tile repair runs $475 to $1,110 installed in 2026, and the $185 diagnostic visit credits toward whichever fix follows, so it's never added on top of the final invoice.
floor-repair/longboat-key.body_html:
Two repair patterns account for most of what we see on Longboat Key, and neither one looks much like a typical mainland service call. The first is water damage from a neighboring unit in one of the island's mid-rise towers, buildings like Grand Bay or L'Ambiance, where a failed supply line or an overflowing tub two floors up sends water down through the structural slab and stains or lifts the ceiling and flooring below. Association bylaws usually assign financial responsibility to the unit where the leak started, but figuring out who pays is a separate question from getting the affected floor repair done, and we treat the two as unrelated from day one, the same approach we describe on the condo flooring page.

The second pattern is cracked or hollow-sounding tile in a guest-facing unit, common in the rental and second-home inventory scattered through Bay Isles, Country Club Shores and the Longboat Key Club area. A cracked porcelain tile or a section of grout that's failed near a shower threshold is a bigger problem in a unit that gets shown to renters or visiting family than it would be in a full-time home, so these calls tend to get scheduled faster than a typical repair. A 1,200 sq ft rental-ready condo with six cracked tiles along a hallway, the kind of thing a departing tenant might report after move-out, is a realistic example of what we're usually asked to fix here, and we tap the surrounding tile first to tell whether it's an isolated crack or a wider bond failure before quoting the job.

Because the whole island carries an AE or VE flood designation, we also get repair calls after a storm event that didn't reach full flood stage but still pushed water under a slider or through a balcony door. Engineered hardwood in an upper-floor unit that took on a few hours of standing water usually shows gapping or cupping at the affected planks rather than full-floor failure, and cupped planks near an exterior wall often recover once the unit dries out properly, a point we cover in our post on whether cupped hardwood floors can be fixed without replacing them. Our overview of Longboat Key's housing stock explains why tower repairs and villa repairs look so different from each other. Every repair quote here starts with the same $185 diagnostic visit we'd run on the mainland, credited toward whatever the fix turns out to be.
floor-repair/longboat-key.cost_html: A guest-facing condo repair after a neighbor's leak, six cracked porcelain tiles at $95-$185 each, runs $570-$1,110 in 2026, with the $185 diagnostic visit credited toward that total rather than added on top. Regrouting the surrounding field, if the existing grout doesn't match cleanly after tile replacement, adds $3.50-$7.00 per sq ft. A cupped or gapped engineered-hardwood repair after minor storm intrusion prices per plank at $95-$225, so an eight-plank fix near a slider door runs $760-$1,800. Work billed outside these categories runs at our $95 hourly rate. Every repair category, tile through hardwood, is priced out on our floor repair cost guide.

faqs.q: Who pays for floor repair after a leak from the unit above mine on Longboat Key?
faqs.a: Association bylaws typically make the unit where the leak started financially responsible, but on Longboat Key we still diagnose and repair the affected floor right away rather than waiting for that question to get sorted out between owners and insurers.

faqs.q: Why does my Longboat Key condo tile sound hollow near the shower?
faqs.a: It's usually a grout or bond failure at the tile threshold rather than a cracked tile itself, something we see often in the island's rental and second-home units where a shower gets more turnover traffic than a full-time home would.

faqs.q: Can hardwood floors recover after storm water gets under a slider on Longboat Key?
faqs.a: Often, yes, if the water is minor and the unit dries out quickly. Gapped or cupped planks near an exterior wall or balcony door frequently settle back down once humidity normalizes, though planks that stay cupped after a few weeks usually need replacement.
